appalling

uh-PAWL-ing — related to 'pale'; something appalling is shocking enough to make you turn pale. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Appalling is awful, terrible, or frightful.

The appalling conditions inside the abandoned factory shocked the safety inspectors.

Worked Example

Health officials visit a rented apartment building and find exposed wiring, no working smoke detectors, and rooms crowded with far more tenants than the building was ever designed to hold.

Conditions that shocking and dangerous are exactly what appalling means. Unlike 'unpleasant,' which is mild, appalling describes something so terrible it provokes genuine horror.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shocking: Shocking means causing a sudden jolt of surprise and disgust -- the emphasis is on the surprise. Appalling needs no surprise at all: a long-familiar horror is still appalling, because appalling measures the horror something provokes, not how unexpected it is.

abysmal: Abysmal measures how wretchedly low in quality something is -- an abysmal test score, abysmal service. Appalling adds moral shock: not merely that a thing is bad, but that seeing it horrifies people.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

delightful: causing great pleasure or enjoyment

admirable: deserving respect and approval

Where it sits · how much shock and fear it causes — dreadful → appalling → horrifying

dreadful vs. appalling: Dreadful is a bit milder than appalling -- dreadful can describe something merely very bad, while appalling implies genuine shock and horror.

horrifying vs. appalling: Horrifying can feel even stronger than appalling: appalling emphasizes moral shock and disgust, while horrifying often adds real fear on top of that.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ap-

prefix — ap-: to, toward (variant of Latin ad-, via Old French a-)

root — -pall-

root — -pall-: pale (Latin (pallere))

suffix — -ing

suffix — -ing: forming an adjective from a verb (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Old French apalir meant 'to grow pale,' from Latin pallere ('to be pale') -- ap- ('to') + -pall- ('pale') -- and the -ing ending turns that verb into a describing word. Something appalling is shocking enough to drain the color from your face.

Use the root in a new word: pallid

Use the root in a new word: pallid: His pallid face suggested he hadn't slept in days.

Word Choice

Appalling is a strong word, usually reserved for conditions, behavior, or events serious enough to provoke real shock or moral outrage.
